>

> or

I actually have planned for a while to make a Succubus Club deck. I want
it to be a necromancy weenie deck (unfortunately there is a total of...
one necro weeny?) so it has the fault of not actually having existing
vampires to create its effect. I would have to put in plenty of skill
cards. And the only other real card would be Jar the Soul (and a handful
of deflections, computer hackings and combat ends effects).

The trick I realized if you wish to get pool from people to do their
dirty work is it has to rely on extortionist tactics. It isn't enough to
offer to harrass peoples vampires, it has to be more compelling. My
thought was always, "Look... give me (2 to 4) pool and I will tap out
your prey, or if you are unwilling to match my price, well, I'll tap
*you* out. It's an offer you can't refuse."

I'm sure that tactic would work very nicely for a combat deck.

Of course, I understand that my deck concept would never have a chance
of winning, but it would fun to try.

It is fun, but the Meth you try to "convince" to match your interest
will do his worst to oust you...
No one of the ancients will let himselve be forced into a certain course
of action without striking back.

> I'm sure that tactic would work very nicely for a combat deck.
>

Which means that you need to stuff some SERIOUS combat cards in your
deck, which means that you could use less Jar the Souls which means that
your intimidation won't work for long.If you mean "combat deck" for the
deck you want to tap out... he'll just eliminate you first.

> Of course, I understand that my deck concept would never have a chance
>
> of winning, but it would fun to try.

Succubus Club is far more effective with

- Setites (you offer the corrupted minions on the open market)
- Ravnos (you offer the stolen equipment on the open market)
- Camarilla Vote Domination decks (you offer pool for boons just to get
rid of enough pool to pull off a Parity Shift)
- Malkavian Decks (you buy the special cards you need to support your
vamps out-of-clan disciplines and pay with a granted Malk Prank Win)
- Bribed Vote decks (to collect and distribute boons)
- Brujah Arms dealer decks (you sell equipment and Allies)
- any intriguing deck trying to manipulate other's

Michael Beer

Messages.Body:
In article <353B50...@bcpress.com>, daniel frey <daniel_freydamnspam
@bcpress.com> writes

>I actually have planned for a while to make a Succubus Club deck. I want
>it to be a necromancy weenie deck (unfortunately there is a total of...
>one necro weeny?) so it has the fault of not actually having existing

>of deflections, computer hackings and combat ends effects).
>

>The trick I realized if you wish to get pool from people to do their
>dirty work is it has to rely on extortionist tactics. It isn't enough to
>offer to harrass peoples vampires, it has to be more compelling. My
>thought was always, "Look... give me (2 to 4) pool and I will tap out
>your prey, or if you are unwilling to match my price, well, I'll tap
>*you* out. It's an offer you can't refuse."

How about altering it to a Presence weenie? Use Mind Numb instead of
Jar the Soul. You have the Combat Ends effect (Majesty), Computer
Hacking or a presence bleed could be used. A few Social Charms and
Enchant Kindred bleeds for pool gain as well as bleeding could be
useful. Deflection is difficult though it wouldn't have been quite as
easy concentrating on necro weenies since, like you say, there aren't
many of them though they do often have Dominate... :(

It might work well with Lena Rowe, Hadrian Garrick and Nepata to give
you a little Obfuscate as well, and then have a few like Delilah Easton,
Gideon Fontaine, Violette Prentis, Mariana Gilbert, Antoinette DuChamp
(her drawback doesn't count for anything here) and maybe a few Obfuscate
weenies - Basil, Dimple, Dan Murdock.

And obviously, with your pool gain you can probably afford a couple of
weapons for defence - maybe a nice .44 Magnum or two.

--
